subject: set directory for compiling model code on  a cluster

messages.author: 18b59f54a8fc6759
messages.subject: set directory for compiling model code on  a cluster
parts:
Dear group,

i'm trying to run the "Eight schools" example on a cluster computer using Rmpi (before i start with my code). My problem is that the stan code is apparently compiled on each node in the /tmp but this is limited to 100Mo and then it crashes. So I would like to define the path where the code should be compiled. I've tried using save_dso=FALSE but it didn't work. Is there a way to define the path where to compile the code?

Thanks!

Sylvain

R script (try_rstan.R):
library(rstan)
library(foreach)
cl <- makeCluster()
print(clusterCall(cl, function() Sys.info()))

schools_code <- '
  data {
    int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
    real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
    real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
  }
  parameters {
    real mu;
    real<lower=0> tau;
    real eta[J];
  }
  transformed parameters {
    real theta[J];
      for (j in 1:J)
      theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
    }
  model {
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
  }
'

schools_dat <- list(J = 8,
y = c(28, 8, -3, 7, -1, 1, 18, 12),
sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11, 9, 11, 10, 18))

a <- foreach(i=1:16) %dopar% {
library(rstan)
fit <- stan(model_code = schools_code, data = schools_dat, save_dso = FALSE,iter = 1000, chains = 4) #doesn't work for save_dso = TRUE neither...

save(fit, file=paste("try",i,".Rdata", sep=""))
}

stopCluster(cl)

PBS file:
#!/bin/csh
#PBS -q parallel32
#PBS -l select=2:ncpus=8:mpiprocs=8

source /usr/share/modules/init/csh
module purge
module load intel-comp/12.1.5

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] set directory for compiling model code on a cluster
parts:
The underlying compiling c++ code is done by package inline, so where the file is created is not configurable by rstan itself.  The save_dso is option is for saving the binary object using R's raw object so it can be saved by R's save/load mechanism. 

However, I think package inline using tempfile() to create those temporary files.  So if we change the returned value of function tempdir(), it can be somehow changed.   Checking out the help of tempdir(), one way worth trying is to set an environment variable TMPDIR that points to a writable directory *before* starting R. 

--
Jiqiang

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: set directory for compiling model code on  a cluster
parts:
On Friday, August 2, 2013 2:54:13 PM UTC-4, Sylvain Bonhommeau wrote:
i'm trying to run the "Eight schools" example on a cluster computer using Rmpi (before i start with my code). My problem is that the stan code is apparently compiled on each node in the /tmp but this is limited to 100Mo and then it crashes.

In general, with the parallel stuff, you want to compile the model once, pass that stanfit object to each of the workers, and collect the output with the sflist2stanfit() function. There help page for sflist2stanfit has an example. In short, you want to do

library(rstan)
library(foreach)
cl <- makeCluster()
print(clusterCall(cl, function() Sys.info()))

schools_code <- '
  data {
    int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
    real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
    real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
  }
  parameters {
    real mu;
    real<lower=0> tau;
    real eta[J];
  }
  transformed parameters {
    real theta[J];
      for (j in 1:J)
      theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
    }
  model {
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
  }
'

schools_dat <- list(J = 8,
y = c(28, 8, -3, 7, -1, 1, 18, 12),
sigma = c(15, 10, 16, 11, 9, 11, 10, 18))
fit <- stan(model_code = schools_code, data = schools_dat, chains = 0) # create an empty stanfit object

stan(fit = fit, iter = 1000, chain_id = i, seed = 12345) # update empty object 16 ways
}
a <- sflist2stanfit(a) # create stanfit object with 16 chains
stopCluster(cl)
 
Ben

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: set directory for compiling model code on a cluster
parts:
Good that it works for some reason.  But if the model gets executed on multiple modes, a temporary binary file of the dynamic shared object still needs to be created in folder returned tempdir().  So you might still have the problem you have before.   

--
Jiqiang
